result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.node_boundary()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the nodes outside a set that are adjacent to it. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L55703-L55754){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.node_boundary( S, T=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Node boundary](/assets/graphs/node-boundary.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same graph and set S. The nodes outside S with a neighbor inside it are D and E, in accent; F and G are further away. The call returns their node ids, 4 and 5." width="100%"} The node boundary of `S` is every node not in `S` that has a neighbor in `S`: the first ring around the set. With `T=`, only boundary nodes in `T` are kept. On a directed graph, these are the nodes `S` points to. Boundaries describe the frontier of a region, the next nodes to infect or inform from a seed set, or the contacts that separate a group from the rest. Matches NetworkX's `node_boundary()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [S]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [T]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optionally restrict the boundary to these nodes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sorted IDs of the boundary nodes. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `S=` is empty or a node does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The boundary of one triangle in the two-triangle graph is the single node across the bridge: ::: {#ba644374 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in graph.node_boundary(["A", "B", "C"])] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['D'] ``` ::: :::
